title: Tech View has its own column choice, separate from List, saved per user
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. Via New Work Order, create several work orders and set a Lead Technician on each, spread across the technicians with some left Unassigned; then open the Work Orders page.
  4. Second device/browser and a second location available.
custom_steps:
1. In List, turn a couple of optional columns on/off.
  2. Switch to Tech View and confirm the same columns.
  3. Log out/in, open on a second device, and change location; confirm the selection persists in both List and Tech View.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Tech View has its own optional-column selection, separate from List: changing columns in one never changes the other.
  • The Tech View column selection is saved per user across logout/login, devices and locations; List keeps saving its columns as it does today.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10048 — Choose what is shown (fields and columns). Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S5-R1, S5-R8 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R1: “Tech View has its own optional-column selection, separate from List. Changing columns in Tech View never changes List, and changing columns in List never changes Tech View.”
  • S5-R8: “Save the Tech View column selection per user across logout/login, devices, and locations. List keeps saving its columns exactly as it does today.”
